<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches sources from the official JetBrains downloads URL (https://download.jetbrains.com/webide/...), which is a trustworthy upstream for PHPStorm. The source array includes a .tar.gz file and a desktop entry, both with provided SHA256 checksums. During the specified commands (`makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`), only source extraction and PKGBUILD parsing occur. No dangerous operations like `eval`, `base64`, or network requests outside the declared source are present. The `rsync` calls in package functions copy files from the extracted archive without executing untrusted code. While the `package_phpstorm-eap-jre` function declares a URL (https://github.com/JetBrains/JetBrainsRuntime), this is unused in the source fetching step, as it relies on the extracted `jbr` directory instead.

The PKGBUILD contains no obfuscated code, unexpected file operations, or supply-chain attack patterns. The described workflow aligns with standard AUR packaging practices. No evidence of injected malicious behavior exists in source fetching or PKGBUILD parsing.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>Source fetching from verified JetBrains URLs with valid checksums poses no immediate risk.</summary>
</security_assessment>

<details>

The `Exec` line points to `/opt/phpstorm-eap/bin/phpstorm` with `%f` for file arguments, which is the standard installation path and usage pattern for JetBrains products on Linux. The `"` HTML entity encoding for quotes in the `Exec` line is standard practice in desktop files. All fields (`Name`, `Icon`, `Comment`, `Categories`, `Terminal`, `StartupNotify`, `StartupWMClass`) are typical and expected values for a JetBrains IDE desktop entry. There are no security concerns.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>Standard JetBrains PhpStorm desktop entry file; no security issues found.</summary>
